children: Lynas Rare Earths produced more than expected in 1Q, and fetched a better-than-anticipated price, says Morgan Stanley. Neodymium and praseodymium output is 1.1% higher than consensus, while total rare-earth oxide output is a 17% beat. "Better concentrate quality supported downstream production," MS says. A realized price of A$102.1/kilogram is 5.1% above consensus, it notes. Sales lagged production, but that is "consistent with timing/inventory build," says the bank. It has an overweight rating on Lynas, with a A$14.65/share target. The stock is up 1.8% at A$12.74. (rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com; @RhiannonHoyle)
